dialogues.speaker: Rakitina
dialogues.text: How's the Kresnik's Torch running today, then...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: How is the torch running today?

dialogues.speaker: Rakitina
dialogues.text: Judging by the sound, the exhaust pipes are a little clogged... Fortunately, it hasn't caused any real performance issues, but I'll need to figure out a way to clear them out...

dialogues.speaker: Rakitina
dialogues.text: Hehe, honestly, this Kresnik's Torch isn't even considered big. The largest one of them all is running right beneath the Snezhnograd!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: So there are a lot of Kresnik's Torches spread across Snezhnaya...

dialogues.speaker: Rakitina
dialogues.text: Yes. After all, relying on a single mega torch to radiate heat across the entire permafrost was proven to be nothing but a pipe dream...

dialogues.speaker: Rakitina
dialogues.text: So Snezhnaya maps out its habitable zones by using the torches as local nodes, and the trains and railways as lines connecting them together.

dialogues.speaker: Rakitina
dialogues.text: This way it can cut out the massive heat loss from long-distance transport.

dialogues.speaker: Rakitina
dialogues.text: Don't worry, it'll be fine. As an administrator for the Energy Commission, this sort of thing is second nature to me.
